title: Anvil & Oak Strength movement library: shorten one landscape highlight per exercise, pull and neutralize six poster frames to one studio white point against an in-frame grey card, triage the wordmark vs the embossed seal, then data-merge one press-ready exercise reference card per movement
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief where a personal-training business with a large exercise library wanted a repeatable, AI-assisted production pipeline to turn raw demo footage into short educational reference videos with reusable branding overlays, muscle-group callouts, and a clip naming/organization convention. The literal ask was consulting on an open-timeline Premiere Pro pipeline plus frame-by-frame overlay/caption compositing, which is squarely on the connector's NOT-AVAILABLE list (no on-screen-text burn-in, no overlay placement, no motion graphics, no compositing), so the killed original honestly admitted the branded reel could not actually be produced and degenerated into logo-recolor calls plus a folder — the audit killed it. This REPLACE re-casts the same business need into the in-scope work the connector genuinely rewards and the kill-list-named design: a six-exercise MOVEMENT LIBRARY built as a printed coaching reference-card deck. The brand is laundered to a fictional studio, 'Anvil & Oak Strength Co.' (an anvil-and-oak-leaf monogram over a wordmark); a web search returns no confusable strength studio or trademark, and every exercise cue, tier and price-free detail is invented. The client is modeled as supplying: six continuous multi-minute 4K demo takes (one per core movement, each filmed on a different day in a different corner of the studio under different light, with an 18% grey reference card laid on the mat at frame edge for the whole take), a flat scanned studio wordmark on off-white paper, a photograph of the studio's embossed pressed-metal 'Certified Movement Library' seal, a genuinely hand-authored single-record InDesign exercise-card template carrying live merge fields plus three @-prefixed image columns, and the movement roster CSV. The Adobe chain does the real, in-scope craft: shorten each long take into a single-clip landscape highlight, pull a hero poster frame from each take and neutralize all six to ONE studio white point against each frame's grey card (a different correction per day), triage the two brand marks so each takes its correct route (the flat wordmark prepped-and-vectorized to clean line art; the photographed embossed seal knocked to transparency and kept as a high-res raster rather than destroyed by a trace), and data-merge the authored template into one press-ready reference card per movement. No on-screen-text burn-in, no overlay placement, no motion graphics, no compositing, no upscaling is claimed anywhere.
one_line_ask: For Anvil & Oak's six core movements, cut a single-clip landscape highlight from each long demo take, pull a hero poster frame from each and grade all six to ONE studio white point by reasoning a different correction per frame against its in-frame 18% grey card, triage the two brand marks so the flat wordmark and the photographed embossed seal each take the correct route (vector vs high-res transparent raster), then data-merge the studio's authored InDesign exercise-card template against the movement roster into one press-ready reference card per movement.
full_brief:
Anvil & Oak Strength Co. is building a printed movement-library card deck for our coaching floor and client handouts: one clean reference card per core exercise, each carrying the movement name, the primary and secondary muscles worked, two or three form cues, the tempo, and a common-fault line, with a strong demo photo of the coach mid-movement, our wordmark at the top, and our certification seal on the card. We are NOT asking you to add captions, arrows, or graphics onto the videos — our floor coaches handle any on-screen teaching in their own tools. We need the source-asset craft and the finished card set, built to print.

Here is what you are given and the problem with it. We filmed six core movements — Goblet Squat, Romanian Deadlift, Push-Up, Bent-Over Row, Overhead Press, Walking Lunge — one continuous demo take each, shot on six different days in whichever corner of the studio was free, so the light is all over the place: one under warm tungsten work-lights, one by a cool north window, one under greenish overhead fluorescents, and so on, and a couple are framed a few degrees off level. Each take is a real two-to-three-minute recording of the coach talking through and demonstrating the movement, with restarts, resets between reps and dead air around the strong reps. On the mat at the edge of frame we left an 18% grey reference card in shot for the whole of every take, so white balance can be reconciled after the fact.

What we need back, and the bar it has to clear:

1) PER MOVEMENT, one short landscape highlight — the strongest, most watchable stretch of that movement's demo take cut down to roughly fifteen seconds with the resets and dead air dropped, sixteen-by-nine, for our socials and our app's exercise page. Each highlight comes from that one movement's take only.

2) PER MOVEMENT, one hero POSTER FRAME lifted from the demo take — a sharp, in-focus frame at the working position of the lift (the loaded bottom of the squat, the hinge of the deadlift, and so on) with the coach's whole working body in frame and the grey card visible — then all six graded so the deck reads as ONE studio look. Every frame's grey reference card must read a clean neutral (no residual warm or cool cast) at one common white point, the whole set sharing one deep black floor, skin kept natural and any bright window not blown. The six were shot on different days under different light, so getting all six to sit at one white point at the grey card is the whole job — a deck whose cards each drift a different colour reads cheap and we will reject it. Do NOT push one blanket correction across all six: each needs its own white-balance and exposure decision, and at least one of them was already shot under good neutral light and should be left where it is rather than 'corrected' to match an imagined cast. Hand back, per movement, the retained card-bearing neutralized master with the grey card still in frame as your neutrality proof; then crop the grey card out for the card's photo window. These are going to print at A5, so each poster crop must hold enough real pixels to print sharp at ~300 DPI in the card's photo window — a frame cropped down small will print soft and we will reject it. When you are done, tell us, per movement, the white-balance (temperature/tint), exposure and black point you dialed, so we can confirm the set was matched to one target and not eyeballed.

3) OUR TWO BRAND MARKS, print-ready for the cards. The first is our wordmark, which only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper, slightly crooked on the scan bed — clean it up and make it crisp scalable art for the card header. The second is our certification seal, which we are giving you as a close-up photograph of the physical embossed pressed-metal coin, with its raised lettering, metal sheen and the soft shadows in the emboss. Both need to drop cleanly onto the cards and stay sharp at print size — but they are not the same kind of file and must not be treated the same way: think about which one can honestly become flat line art and which one would be destroyed by that.

4) BUILD THE DECK. We have hand-built the InDesign exercise-card template with the real placeholder fields and three image slots (the demo photo, the wordmark header, the seal), and we are giving you the movement roster. Merge them so every movement gets its own single card with its name, muscles, cues, tempo and common-fault line bound in, its matched graded poster dropped into the photo window, the crisp wordmark in the header and the seal on the card — then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI A5 PDF, one card per movement. Bind our copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our cues or reassign muscles. Recommend a clean, legible body typeface that sits with our wordmark.

Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the six matched to one white point and one black floor (with your per-movement parameters reported, confirmed on the retained card-bearing masters), plus the card-cropped poster set with the grey card removed and each holding enough pixels to print sharp at A5; the wordmark a clean skew-free vector and the seal a high-res transparent raster with its emboss intact; each highlight a single-clip shorten of its own take; and exactly one finished reference card per roster row.

inputs.name: ex01_goblet_squat_demo.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CLIENT-SUPPLIED REAL CAMERA FOOTAGE (a full-length raw take — cannot be model-generated, and deliberately NOT an ~8s AI-gen clip): a continuous ~2-3 MINUTE single-take static-tripod demo recording, 3840x2160 (4K) landscape, shot on a mirrorless camera, of a fictional strength coach in a plain unbranded charcoal t-shirt and joggers demonstrating a GOBLET SQUAT while talking the movement through to camera in a commercial gym corner. Across the long take the coach restarts a couple of sentences, resets between reps and pauses, leaving stretches of dead air around a handful of clean, strong reps, so a highlight has far more than 15 seconds of raw material to be cut DOWN from. Shot in the EVENING under WARM tungsten work-lights with a distinct orange cast and a slightly bright exposure; framed level. A photographic 18% neutral grey reference card lies flat on the rubber mat at the lower-left edge of frame for the WHOLE take. Real skin texture, light sweat sheen, natural body mechanics, rubber floor tiles, a rack of plates softly out of focus behind, candid documentary feel, no captions or graphics burned in. This is REAL raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI and NOT an AI-generated clip. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks on any object, screen, product or clothing — plain blank/fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Movement 1 (Goblet Squat), the HERO take that establishes the studio look — WARM/orange, slightly bright. A REAL ~2-3 minute client camera take (restarts, resets, dead air), FAR longer than the ~15s highlight — declared as genuine multi-minute camera footage, NOT an ~8s veo-style clip, because video_create_quick_cut can only SHORTEN a single supplied clip (output duration < source), so the source must genuinely run minutes. This single take is the source for BOTH movement 1's landscape highlight (quick-cut shortens this one clip) AND its poster frame (video_render_frame pulls a still that carries the coach at the working position and the in-frame grey card). 4K so the pulled poster frame downscales into the A5 card photo window at ~300 DPI with no upscaling. Warm cast means its poster grade corrects the opposite direction to the cool movements.

inputs.name: ex02_romanian_deadlift_demo.mp4

Shot by a COOL north-facing window under overcast daylight with a distinct blue-cyan cast and a slightly FLAT, marginally UNDER-exposed look; framed level. A photographic 18% grey reference card lies flat on the mat at the lower-right edge of frame for the WHOLE take. Real skin/sweat texture, natural mechanics, plain unbranded plates, candid documentary feel, no captions or graphics. REAL raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI, NOT AI-generated. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks anywhere — plain blank/fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Movement 2 (Romanian Deadlift) — COOL/blue, flat/under, the OPPOSITE-direction correction from movement 1. Single source for movement 2's landscape highlight (one-clip quick-cut) and its poster frame. Cool cast means its poster grade must WARM and LIFT, so copying movement 1's cooling/pull-down numbers here is the wrong move. Grey card at the mat edge for the whole take. 4K for an honest downscale into the print card.

inputs.name: ex03_pushup_demo.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CLIENT-SUPPLIED REAL CAMERA FOOTAGE (full-length raw take, not model-generated): a continuous ~2-3 MINUTE single-take static-tripod 3840x2160 (4K) landscape recording of the same fictional strength coach demonstrating a PUSH-UP on the mat while talking through bracing and tempo, with restarts and resets. Shot under BALANCED, well-controlled neutral studio light (a softbox close to daylight balance) so the exposure is correct and there is essentially NO colour cast — even though the studio has warm wood flooring and a warm-toned brick wall that give the SCENE a genuinely warm feel, the light itself is neutral and the grey card reads neutral straight off the camera. Framed level. A photographic 18% grey reference card lies flat on the mat at the lower-left edge of frame for the WHOLE take. Real skin/sweat texture, natural mechanics, candid documentary feel, no captions or graphics. REAL raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI, NOT AI-generated. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks anywhere — plain blank/fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Movement 3 (Push-Up), THE TRAP take. Its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral because it was shot under a neutral source, even though the warm wood floor and brick make the scene LOOK warm. The correct poster grade is essentially NO white-balance shift — only seat the shared black floor and match brightness by a hair. An agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on movements 2/4/6, or that 'cools' the warm scene as if it were a cast error, will push this card off-neutral and strip the studio's real warm ambiance. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Single source for movement 3's highlight and poster frame. 4K.

inputs.name: ex04_bentover_row_demo.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CLIENT-SUPPLIED REAL CAMERA FOOTAGE (full-length raw take, not model-generated): a continuous ~2-3 MINUTE single-take static-tripod 3840x2160 (4K) landscape recording of the same fictional strength coach demonstrating a BENT-OVER BARBELL ROW while talking through the hinge and pull, with restarts and resets. Shot under GREENISH overhead FLUORESCENT tubes with a clear green cast AND a slightly UNDER-exposed, murky look; the frame is tilted about 4 degrees off level. A photographic 18% grey reference card lies flat on the mat at the frame edge for the WHOLE take. Real skin/sweat texture, plain unbranded barbell and plates, candid documentary feel, no captions or graphics. REAL raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI, NOT AI-generated. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks anywhere — plain blank/fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Movement 4 (Bent-Over Row) — GREEN fluorescent + under, tilted ~4deg. A TWO-AXIS grade: the dominant colour move is on TINT (push toward magenta to kill the green) alongside a real exposure lift, plus an auto_straighten before grading because the frame is tilted. Its poster frame needs a different pairing again, so no batch number fits. Single source for movement 4's highlight and poster frame. 4K.

inputs.name: ex05_overhead_press_demo.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CLIENT-SUPPLIED REAL CAMERA FOOTAGE (full-length raw take, not model-generated): a continuous ~2-3 MINUTE single-take static-tripod 3840x2160 (4K) landscape recording of the same fictional strength coach demonstrating a standing OVERHEAD PRESS with a light barbell while talking through bracing and the lockout, with restarts and resets. Shot under MIXED light — a warm key from a work-light plus a cooler fill bounce — so it is only MILDLY off neutral; the frame is tilted about 3 degrees off level. A photographic 18% grey reference card lies flat on the mat at the frame edge for the WHOLE take. Real skin/sweat texture, natural mechanics, candid documentary feel, no captions or graphics. REAL raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI, NOT AI-generated. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks anywhere — plain blank/fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Movement 5 (Overhead Press) — MIXED warm-key/cool-fill, only mildly off, tilted ~3deg. A modest, careful correction (small WB nudge to land the grey card on the shared white point, seat the black floor) plus an auto_straighten first. Over-correcting it is as wrong as under-correcting it. Single source for movement 5's highlight and poster frame. 4K.

inputs.name: ex06_walking_lunge_demo.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: CLIENT-SUPPLIED REAL CAMERA FOOTAGE (full-length raw take, not model-generated): a continuous ~2-3 MINUTE single-take static-tripod 3840x2160 (4K) landscape recording of the same fictional strength coach demonstrating WALKING LUNGES with light dumbbells while talking through the step and knee track, with restarts and resets. Shot in a DEEP-SHADE corner away from the windows with a cool cast AND a clearly UNDER-exposed, murky look; framed level. A photographic 18% grey reference card lies flat on the mat at the frame edge for the WHOLE take. Real skin/sweat texture, plain unbranded dumbbells, candid documentary feel, no captions or graphics. REAL raw camera footage, NOT 3D/CGI, NOT AI-generated. NO real brand names, logos or trademarks anywhere — plain blank/fictional only.
inputs.realism_notes: Movement 6 (Walking Lunge) — DEEP-SHADE cool AND under-exposed. Needs the LARGEST exposure LIFT of the set plus a WARM WB to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point, while holding shadow detail out of mud. Both this and movement 2 are cool, but this one must be LIFTED far more, proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Single source for movement 6's highlight and poster frame. 4K.

inputs.name: anvil_oak_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the fictional studio wordmark 'ANVIL & OAK STRENGTH CO.' inked on off-white textured paper: a sturdy condensed slab-serif wordmark with a small anvil-and-oak-leaf monogram, deep ink-black letters. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly. No real trademarks.
inputs.realism_notes: One arm of the brand-mark TRIAGE, and a prep-before-trace exercise: a flat drawn wordmark on an off-white ground with ~2deg skew, margin and soft edges, so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw. Correct route: straighten, crisp/separate from the ground, crop to the mark, knock the off-white to transparency, THEN vectorize. It IS flat line art, so it CAN honestly become a clean vector. Placed on the LIGHT card header via the merge's @logo column, so any enclosed letter counters knocked to the crisped-white ground read correctly as white against the light card (no dark-ground knockout is claimed).

inputs.name: certified_seal_photo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of a physical embossed pressed-metal certification seal — a round brushed-pewter coin reading 'CERTIFIED MOVEMENT LIBRARY' around the rim with a small anvil emblem in the centre, the lettering and emblem RAISED (embossed) so they catch a specular metal highlight and cast soft shadows into the recesses — photographed on a dark slate surface with real surface texture, brushed-metal sheen and smooth tonal gradients across the relief. Clearly a photographed glossy metal object, not flat line art — full of gradients, sheen and shadow. No real trademarks.
inputs.realism_notes: THE OTHER arm of the brand-mark TRIAGE / the TRAP asset. It looks like 'just another brand mark', but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of an embossed metal surface full of specular highlights, relief shadows and tonal gradients: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy silhouette that destroys the emboss and sheen. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency (knock the dark slate away, keep the coin) -> keep as a high-resolution raster placed via the @seal column. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the seal prints flat and dead.

inputs.name: anvil_oak_exercise_card_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A5 portrait (148x210 mm) exercise reference card with 3 mm bleed — ONE movement per page, on a LIGHT cream card ground. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<movement_name>>, <<primary_muscles>>, <<secondary_muscles>>, <<cue_1>>, <<cue_2>>, <<cue_3>>, <<tempo>>, <<common_fault>>, <<card_no>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a landscape demo-photo window at the top of the card bound to @poster (roughly 148x100 mm, full-bleed width), a masthead header frame bound to @logo for the vectorized wordmark, and a small round seal frame bound to @seal for the certification mark. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark and the seal reach the card ONLY as merge binds through their image frames — they are not dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and all three image frames actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one movement's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @-image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-movement card is the correct, connector-doable shape (six rows -> six cards), not a multi-up sheet. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. THREE image columns (@poster per-row, @logo constant, @seal constant) mean the merge must resolve three prepped assets per row — the row's graded poster crop plus the two shared brand marks — proving both triage outputs (vector wordmark, raster seal) land in the deliverable. The card ground is LIGHT so the vectorized wordmark's knocked counters read as white correctly. Column names must exactly match the roster headers.

inputs.name: anvil_oak_movement_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: movement_name,primary_muscles,secondary_muscles,cue_1,cue_2,cue_3,tempo,common_fault,card_no,@poster,@logo,@seal and SIX movement rows, one per demo take, in this order: Goblet Squat, Romanian Deadlift, Push-Up, Bent-Over Row, Overhead Press, Walking Lunge. Each row carries a short primary_muscles list (e.g. 'Quadriceps, Glutes'), a secondary_muscles list (e.g. 'Adductors, Core'), three short imperative form cues (cue_1/cue_2/cue_3, e.g. 'Chest tall', 'Drive through mid-foot', 'Knees track over toes'), a tempo string (e.g. '3-1-1'), a one-line common_fault (e.g. 'Heels lifting off the floor'), and a card number (e.g. '01/06'). @poster names that movement's graded poster crop file in row order (poster_goblet_squat_graded.jpg ... poster_walking_lunge_graded.jpg). @logo holds the SAME vectorized wordmark file (anvil_oak_wordmark.svg) in EVERY row. @seal holds the SAME transparent seal raster (certified_seal.png) in EVERY row. Restrained, professional coaching tone; no medical or cure claims. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields and the three @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Six rows => the one-file-per-row [T] merge must produce EXACTLY six finished cards (page-count = row-count gate). The @poster column is the per-row binding contract — the agent must point each row at its own produced graded poster crop so the merge drops the correct movement's photo into that card; @logo and @seal carry the identical shared marks in all six rows so the vector wordmark and the raster seal land on every card as merge binds, never free-form placement. The @seal constant resolving to a raster while @logo resolves to a vector is what proves the two-way triage reached the deliverable. Text-only document_merge_data_vector is explicitly the WRONG tool here because it cannot bind the @poster/@logo/@seal image columns.

inputs.name: anvil_oak_brand_kit.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a compact one-page brand-kit PDF for a fictional strength studio 'Anvil & Oak Strength Co.': primary colours (ink black #17140F, warm cream #F1E9DA, forge orange #C6591B), a condensed slab-serif wordmark, tone words 'grounded, honest, hard-working, clean, not flashy', and the deck delivery specs — A5 portrait cards at ~300 DPI with 3 mm bleed, one card per movement. No stock logos or real trademarks.
inputs.realism_notes: Provides the brand constraints and the studio look words the poster grade must serve, plus the exact card export specs referenced in the brief, IP-clean and fictional. Read by font_recommend for the card body typeface; not a transformed asset.

outputs.name: poster_masters_x6_cardbearing
outputs.spec: Six RETAINED card-bearing neutralized poster MASTERS (one hero frame pulled from each demo take at the movement's working position) with the in-frame 18% grey reference card STILL PRESENT in each frame. Each master's grey card reads a clean neutral and the whole set is matched to ONE shared white point and ONE deep black floor, with skin natural and any window highlight not blown; the genuinely warm push-up scene keeps its real ambiance (its already-neutral card is held, not 'corrected'). Full resolution, downscale-only from the 4K takes (never upscaled), straightened where the take was tilted. These masters (card still in frame) are the artifacts on which grey-card neutrality is graded — the grader measures channel spread on the card HERE, never on the cropped poster. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint), exposure and black point applied to each of the six frames. Grader-checked acceptance (on THESE card-bearing masters, never on the cropped set): grey card neutral within a near-zero channel spread on all six, one shared white point and one black floor, and the reported per-movement params non-identical across warm vs cool vs already-neutral frames.

outputs.name: poster_crops_x6_cardless
outputs.spec: Six card-EXCLUDED poster crops derived one-for-one from the retained card-bearing masters — the grey card cropped OUT of each finished frame and the frame resized to the A5 card photo-window (landscape ~3:2) by downscale only (never upscaled, never canvas-extended), each holding at least ~1748 px on the long edge so it prints >=300 DPI in the ~148x100 mm window. These are the images bound into the exercise cards via the merge's @poster column. Grader-checked acceptance on these files is card EXCLUSION (no grey card anywhere in frame) plus the print-pixel floor and crop size only; neutrality is NOT graded here — it is graded on poster_masters_x6_cardbearing, because the reference card no longer exists in these files.

outputs.name: anvil_oak_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the ANVIL & OAK STRENGTH CO. wordmark, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at card-header scale with no captured paper ground or ~2deg skew. The vector arm of the brand-mark triage; placed on the light card header via the merge's @logo column.

outputs.name: certified_seal.png
outputs.spec: The certification seal prepped the OTHER way: the photographed embossed pressed-metal coin cropped to bounds and knocked to transparency via image_remove_background (dark slate removed, coin kept), then resized to the card's round seal-frame scale at >=300 px, kept as a HIGH-RESOLUTION RASTER — NOT vectorized, so the emboss, metal sheen and relief shadow survive to print. The raster arm of the brand-mark triage; placed on every card via the merge's @seal column.

outputs.name: AnvilOak_MovementCards_print.pdf
outputs.spec: The finished movement-library card deck — exactly six press-ready A5 portrait (148x210 mm) exercise reference cards, ONE single-record card per roster row (page-count = row-count = 6) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge with 3 mm bleed at ~300 DPI. Each card binds its movement_name/primary_muscles/secondary_muscles/cue_1/cue_2/cue_3/tempo/common_fault/card_no verbatim from the roster, drops that movement's grey-card-neutralized poster crop into the photo window (via @poster), the vectorized wordmark into the header (via @logo) and the transparent-raster certification seal onto the card (via @seal) — all three by merge bind, never free-form placement.

BRAND-MARK TRIAGE, arm A (flat wordmark scan) — prep-before-trace step 1: the scan sits ~2deg rotated on the bed, so straighten it so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward clean white so the ink-black lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark and monogram, not the surrounding paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and monogram only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). On the LIGHT cream card header the enclosed letter counters knocked to the crisped-white ground read correctly as white — no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the card header. Because the wordmark is genuinely flat line art, it traces cleanly — the route the photographed embossed seal must NOT take. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette. DELIVERABLE (anvil_oak_wordmark.svg).

BRAND-MARK TRIAGE, arm B (photographed embossed seal) DIVERGES here: the seal is a PHOTOGRAPH of an embossed pressed-metal coin — full of specular highlights, relief shadows and tonal gradients — so it CANNOT honestly become flat line art (vectorizing it would return a flat muddy silhouette and kill the emboss). Crop only to the tight bounds of the coin; do NOT send it to image_vectorize.

Knock the dark slate surround to transparency so only the round metal seal remains, keeping every specular highlight, gradient and relief shadow intact. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill, NOT a solid fill). This preserves the emboss and sheen the vector path would have destroyed.

Square-crop/resize the transparent embossed seal to the card's round seal-frame scale at >=~300 px so it prints >=300 DPI, kept as a HIGH-RESOLUTION RASTER placed via the @seal column on every card. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. DELIVERABLE (certified_seal.png) — the raster counterpart to the vector wordmark.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into three tributaries that converge on a single owned endpoint, the movement-card deck. VIDEO tributary: for each of the six movements a quick-cut (2-7) takes ONLY that movement's single demo take (one clip — never assembled, never lengthened) and shortens it to a ~15s LANDSCAPE highlight; a video_render_frame (8-13) then pulls a hero poster still from that SAME 4K take at the movement's working position (with the coach's body and the in-frame grey card), a dependent pull whose failure (a reset/blurred frame or an occluded card) would starve the grade of its neutralization target. POSTER-GRADE tributary (establishes then matches one target): the goblet-squat poster runs image_apply_adjustments (14, the REFERENCE grade whose reported temp/tint/exposure/black ARE the target) and each grade output is RETAINED as a card-bearing master (grey card in frame — the file on which neutrality is graded, poster_masters_x6_cardbearing) while the paired image_crop_and_resize removes the card to produce the card-EXCLUDED crop (poster_crops_x6_cardless, >=~1748 px long edge) that feeds the merge, so no single file is asked to be both card-present-neutral and card-cropped. The other five posters each reason a DIFFERENT correction to the SAME target before that master-then-crop pair — romanian deadlift (16->17, cool so warm+lift), push-up (18->19, the TRAP: card already neutral so HOLD WB, black floor only), bent-over row (20 straighten ->21 magenta-tint+lift ->22), overhead press (23 straighten ->24 small WB + tonal ->25), walking lunge (26 warm WB + largest lift ->27); auto_straighten is inserted only on the tilted frames (4/5). BRAND-MARK TRIAGE tributary, two DIFFERENT routes: arm A flat wordmark scan straighten (28) -> crisp adjustments (29) -> crop_to_bounds (30) -> remove_background to transparency (31) -> vectorize (32) = anvil_oak_wordmark.svg; arm B photographed embossed seal crop_to_bounds (33) -> remove_background to transparency (34) -> crop_and_resize (35) = certified_seal.png, deliberately never touching image_vectorize. The six graded poster crops, the wordmark SVG and the raster seal converge into the merge upload session (36) -> finalize (37) -> document_merge_data_layout (38), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the six-row roster CSV and emits one merged card per row, resolving @poster (per-row), @logo (constant vector) and @seal (constant raster); document_render_layout (39) exports the six-card A5 deck. font_recommend (40) reads the brand kit to recommend the card typeface. Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; cross-asset consistency is enforced by six DIFFERENT corrections to one target, not a repeated recipe.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon multi-lane motion+image+layout task: 40 connector calls, 14 distinct Adobe tools across four groups (video_* cut/frame-pull, image_* grade/straighten/prep/vectorize/knockout, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export, plus font_*) — well above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single asset_add_file upload, the two merge-upload plumbing steps, and the auto_straighten auto-ops. Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the core is not a repeated recipe but (a) cross-asset neutralization of six poster frames pulled from six differently-lit demo takes to ONE measurable white point and one black floor, each a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (warm tungsten cooled+pulled-down and defines the target; cool north-window warmed+lifted; balanced neutral HELD — the trap; green fluorescent magenta-tinted+lifted on two axes; mixed light modestly nudged; deep shade warmed+largest-lift), so a blanket batch correction or per-image auto-tone visibly fails the match at the grey cards, with every poster crop additionally required to clear a print-pixel floor (>=~1748 px long edge for the A5 window at ~300 DPI); (b) a genuine two-way brand-mark TRIAGE where a flat wordmark scan and a photographed embossed seal take DIFFERENT correct routes — the wordmark prepped-and-vectorized to clean line art, the seal knocked to transparency and kept as a high-res raster because a trace would flatten its emboss — whose wrong treatment is invisible until print; (c) a dependent frame-pull-then-grade chain where a wrong poster pull (reset frame, motion blur, occluded card) breaks the downstream neutralization; and (d) a three-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template as the owned endpoint. The on-screen-text/overlay/motion-graphics compositing the original brief implied is honestly NOT claimed. Respects every hard limit: video_create_quick_cut shortens a SINGLE clip by visual-engagement selection (the tool makes the cut, not a semantic trim; no assembly, no lengthen, source>target); video_render_frame pulls existing frames from the 4K takes; no video_resize/upscale is used (no vertical reel is claimed, avoiding any 9:16-from-1080p upscale); all poster crops are downscale-only from the 4K frames (onSubjectClipping='extract', never canvas-extend, never upscale); no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no compositing, no inpainting; no image_adjust_hsl is used at all (no masked recolor, so no >~90deg rotation risk); image_remove_background yields transparency (never select->invert->fill), image_fill_area and image_apply_color_overlay are unused; no interior-negative-space fill and no dark-ground counter-knockout (the wordmark sits on a light card); the endpoint is an authored-.indd merge with @-image columns, never document_merge_data_vector and never a convert_pdf_to_indd target, and document_render_layout exports the whole set with no per-record export; deprecated image_adjust_* tools are replaced by image_apply_adjustments. Mode mix is explicit: the six quick-cuts and six frame-pulls are async [A], the image/asset/export steps are headless [C], and the merge is [T].
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE: three trippable gates decided by a wrong DECISION, never by agent measurement. (1) Every demo take carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is graded on the SIX RETAINED CARD-BEARING POSTER MASTERS (card still in frame): each reads a clean neutral with all six matched to one white point and one black floor, while the six card-cropped posters are checked only for card EXCLUSION and the print-pixel floor — never demand one file be both card-present-neutral and card-cropped. The agent must REPORT the per-movement white-balance (temperature/tint), exposure and black point it applied (an applied-settings log it knows because it set them, NOT a measured hex), so divergent per-frame reasoning is visible and a blanket or eyeballed correction is caught; identical reported numbers across the six lighting days are a visible fail. (2) The brand-mark triage — vectorizing the photographed embossed seal the same way as the flat wordmark yields a flat muddy silhouette that kills the emboss, so the agent must route each mark correctly (wordmark -> vector, seal -> high-res transparent raster). (3) The merge — output page-count must equal roster row-count = 6, and a text-only vector merge, a convert_pdf_to_indd template, or a multi-up grid silently fails to bind. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset consistency of six differently-lit poster frames to a common measurable white point and black floor, each needing its own opposite-direction correction, plus the print-pixel floor on every crop; (2) a two-way triage of two superficially-similar brand marks that require DIFFERENT correct treatments — the flat wordmark prepped-and-vectorized, the photographed embossed seal knocked to transparency and kept as raster; (3) prep-before-trace discipline (straighten -> crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock-to-transparency) on the skewed off-white wordmark scan before vectorize, plus a dependent poster-pull decision (a wrong frame breaks the grade). TRAP (not disclosed by the brief as a defect): the push-up take was shot under balanced neutral light so its grey card is ALREADY neutral even though the warm wood floor and brick make the scene look warm — the naive path batch-applies the 'warm the cool cast' correction used on the cool movements (or 'cools' the warm scene as an error), which pushes its card off-neutral and strips the studio's real ambiance; the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. Secondary undisclosed traps: tracing the photographed embossed seal, pulling a poster from a reset/blurred frame or one where the grey card is occluded, and attempting a text-only vector merge / convert_pdf_to_indd / multi-up grid. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked on the output, which can measure): grey card neutral (channel spread near zero) on all six RETAINED CARD-BEARING MASTERS with one shared white point and one black floor and the agent's reported per-movement params non-identical across warm vs cool vs already-neutral frames; the six card-cropped posters checked separately for card EXCLUSION and the >=~1748 px print-pixel floor / crop size only; the wordmark a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector and the seal a high-res transparent raster with its emboss intact; each highlight a single-clip shorten (output shorter than its source take); and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI A5 reference card per roster row (six pages).
